corpus: the neurag/ tree itself -- versioned by definition, so a result is reproducible from a commit hash alone. bench/ is dropped back out after ingest (run.py:decontaminate).
ground_truth: expect = path suffixes relative to the corpus root. A query is answered if ANY of them appears in the ranking.

rules.identifier: expect = EVERY ingested file containing the query string literally. Mechanical, so it cannot be tuned: tests/test_bench_set.py recomputes it from disk and fails if this file disagrees.
rules.concept: expect = every file a reader would accept as answering the question -- documentation counts, not only the implementing module. Judged by reading, NOT by what a run returned. Frozen at v2; widening it after a miss is how a benchmark becomes decoration.

history.v1: First run scored recall@5 0.800 overall. Six misses; four were authoring errors, not retrieval failures -- v1 listed only implementing modules and ignored the docs that answer the same question, and under-listed identifier hits. Corrected AFTER seeing results, which is stated here rather than hidden: the identifier half is now mechanical and test-enforced, and the concept half is frozen. Two misses survived the correction and are real: q22 and q27.
history.v2: Rules above applied uniformly to all 30 queries.

kinds.identifier: exact strings -- names, flags, env vars, constants. The class vector-only retrieval failed, at 67% recall.
kinds.concept: paraphrase, IT or EN, with no literal overlap with the answer. The class lexical retrieval is blind to.
